# Harrison

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** a crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a queer, fussy, fidgety little man who can be seen sitting in his shirt sleeves on his vine-shaded veranda enjoying a pipe. When caught by surprise or feeling sheepish, he is prone to blushing red in the face.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P5](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0005), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039)_

## Personality

A crusty, crabbed, and outspoken man who admits to being lonesome, Mr. Harrison possesses a sharp temper and an unusual habit of blunt honesty that often offends his neighbors. He takes a pragmatic view of life, prefers keeping to himself without women around his home, and can be quite nervous when caught off guard or when admitting fault. Despite his crusty exterior, he enjoys the youthful energy of Anne Shirley, shows a kind heart toward his pet, and can prove quite mild, friendly, and neighborly once acquainted with others.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P9](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0009), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009)_

## Traits

- Outspoken and blunt  <sub>[v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009)</sub>
- Crusty and crabbed

## History

Before Anne Shirley returned home from Queen's, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables in Avonlea and moved in as a newcomer from New Brunswick. He quickly gained a local reputation as an odd 'crank' for keeping house by himself, lacking set mealtimes, only washing dishes in rain barrels on wet Sundays, and making outspoken remarks to local figures like Mrs. Rachel Lynde. One day, after angrily confronting Anne when her Jersey cow strayed onto his grain, he received a visit from her to confess that she had accidentally sold his cow by mistake. Though initial tension arose when his parrot insulted her, he treated Anne politely, invited her inside, and enjoyed tea with her after she cleared up the misunderstanding and washed his dishes. Over time, Mr. Harrison formed a warm friendship with Anne, engaging in discussions about the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and local affairs on his veranda. During these visits, he frequently voiced his candid opinions on truthfulness and community figures while admitting that spending time with Anne made him feel young again.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P7](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0007), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P4](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0004), [v2 c3 P16](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0016), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P45](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0045), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009), [v2 c9 P11](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0011)_

## Background by volume

- Moved to Avonlea from New Brunswick in early April to buy Robert Bell's farm  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Acquired a swearing parrot named Ginger from his brother, a sailor  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c3 P19](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0019), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038)</sub>
- Married to Emily Harrison

## Quotes

> I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> It was the truth and I believe in telling the truth to everybody.  <sub>[v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005)</sub>

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>
